tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'duo_pose' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'pose': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'duo_hinge' reports the pose, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

pose.description: For 'duo_pose': the pose to move the hinge to.

angle.description: For 'duo_pose' with pose 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Fix the error messages you listed: the ones the app shows for failures the person can do nothing about. Work on a new branch from jusprin-dev. Do not push, and add no merge commits.

The rule is in AGENTS.md, under "Error handling". Read all of it before you start. In short: a person sees a specific sentence only when they can act on it and Kenneth chose that sentence. Every other failure stops the work, goes up unchanged to the handler at the top of its entry point, and is reported through report_unexpected_error (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp). The person then sees only "Something went wrong on our side". A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, and its error text goes to the AI model only. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also sent through report_if_automatic.

Why these messages were missed: the earlier sweep (commit 3c134d39e3 on jusprin-dev, "Report every failure a person cannot act on; keep a sentence only where they can") audited only src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ and Home/, plus the server. Nobody read Shell/, Workspace/ or PrinterSetup/. That commit is the pattern to follow: read its diff to see how it replaced sentences with the generic one and where it put top handlers (reported(...)).

Two of your paths are confirmed in the code on jusprin-dev:
- Chat page: when the page gets a bridge_error from AgentHost.cpp, AgentUI/src/App.tsx calls setCommandError(payload.message), so the host's own text shows in the chat. The host and the page are both our code, so every bridge_error is unexpected: report it on the host side and show the generic sentence. For handshake_required the page also calls created.retry(). Find out whether the person should see anything at all while that retry recovers, and do what the rule says.
- Plates pane: LeftPane::run_command (Shell/LeftPane.cpp) shows result.message in a "Couldn't do that" dialog and only writes a log line. A log line is not a report. This should report and show the generic sentence.

I have not checked the other paths. Confirm each one in the code or in the running app before you change it.

Where the text was written for the AI model (the printer chat's action cards, the setup card's slice estimate, undoing a change, the All settings panel), keep the text for the model, and show the person only that the action failed. Text such as "pass scope printer", "ask again with preempt" or "Read workspace_inspect", or the name "Orca", must not reach the person.

Some messages may be failures the person can fix. Do not build a sentence for those: each needs Kenneth's yes first. Bring them to Kenneth as one question each, saying what the person would see and what they could do. The candidates I saw:
- "Connecting a Bambu Lab printer needs Bambu's network plug-in, which is not loaded"
- "Could not start the client CLI. Use Copy or check its installation."
- "This printer was renamed or removed. Open it again from Printers."
- "Object name cannot be empty" and "Object already has that name" (perhaps the rename box should refuse those names instead)
- "No more plates can be added" (perhaps the add button should be greyed out instead)
Until Kenneth answers, leave those messages as they are.

How to work:
- Reproduce each failure before you fix it, as AGENTS.md and the global rules require: show what the person sees before the fix and after. A failure you cannot reproduce gets no fix; list it.
- Add a test for each fix that fails first and passes after.
- One commit per cause.
- Remove the deleted strings from the catalogs, as the regenerated template and catalogs do.
- Build with -- -j4, after checking uptime and pgrep -fl ninja. Run agent_bridge_tests, jusprin_tests, the AgentUI and HomeUI vitest suites, scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh against jusprin-dev, and the shell harness modes that cover what you changed (the plates pane, the printer chat, printer setup, Preferences › Agent). On jusprin-dev, five modes already fail: --print-issues (7), --print-issue-readers (8), --printer-network-check (2), --printer-connect-skill (3) and --project-prompt-requests (1 to 3). --printer-chat-sheet sometimes crashes while shutting down, on jusprin-dev too.
- Never drive Kenneth's own JusPrin. Use a scratch --datadir. Send nothing to the real Sentry.
</pasted_content id="ef43">

content.text:
Yes, it makes sense. What it says about the code is accurate, and the approach follows the error rules in AGENTS.md. I'd add three things before anyone starts, because each one would otherwise stall the work or change how it turns out.

**What I checked, and it holds:**
- Commit `3c134d39e3` is on `jusprin-dev`, and it is the sweep the brief describes.
- `report_if_automatic` and `reported(...)` exist in `Support/ErrorReport.hpp` and do what the brief says.
- **Chat page:** `App.tsx:127-132` shows the host's `bridge_error` text. For `handshake_required` it also retries, so the banner "A hello handshake is required before other messages." stays on screen even though the retry recovers by itself. The person should probably see nothing in that case, and the brief already asks for this to be checked.
- **Plates pane:** `LeftPane.cpp:211-212` writes a log line and then shows `result.message` under "Couldn't do that". No report is sent.
- All the shell harness modes the brief names exist. I did not run them, so the list of modes that already fail on `jusprin-dev` is unverified.

**What I'd add:**

1. **What counts as reproducing a failure that only a bug causes.** Most of the roughly 110 messages fire only when our own code is wrong. Examples are a page sending a malformed message, or a plate id from an earlier session. Nobody can make those happen by clicking in the real app. Under the bug-fix rule as written, the agent would list most of them as "cannot reproduce" and fix almost nothing. The brief should say whether a shell harness run that forces the failure, or an instrumented page that sends the bad message, counts as the reproduction. It should show what the person sees on screen, not just a failing unit test.

2. **One dialog, not two.** `report_unexpected_error` itself opens the "Something went wrong on our side" dialog. So the plates pane fix should replace the "Couldn't do that" dialog, not show the generic sentence inside it. The brief's wording "report and show the generic sentence" could be read either way.

3. **Two tooling details.**
   - JusPrin's catalogs are updated with `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. `scripts/run_gettext` handles OrcaSlicer's catalogs, which the fork never edits. The brief should name the right one.
   - `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` failed to configure on this Mac earlier today with "Could NOT find LibLZMA". The brief should say what to do if it fails again. Since the work must not be pushed, the CI clang-tidy job can't stand in for it.

The list of questions for Kenneth is reasonable. Each of those messages is a case where the person could plausibly do something, so leaving them alone until he answers is right.

content.text:
Mostly remove them. Swapping each site's text for the generic sentence is the pattern the rules forbid. The rules in AGENTS.md say an unexpected failure gets no code of its own: no catch, no default, and no sentence. It is turned into a thrown error where it happens, and only the one handler at the top of the entry point reports it and shows "Something went wrong on our side". If each site showed the generic sentence itself, there would be 110 places deciding what the person sees, and most of them would still send no report. That's the plates pane today: a log line and a dialog, with nothing sent to us.

So for most sites the change is to keep the check and drop the sentence. Where the code notices the failure, it throws an error that carries the facts, for example "plate id 7 belongs to an earlier session". That text goes into the report for us and is never shown or translated. The top handlers already exist:
- **Chat page messages:** `AgentWebView.cpp:314-317` catches anything thrown while handling a page message and calls `report_unexpected_error`, which opens the generic dialog itself. So in `AgentHost.cpp`, each `send_bridge_error("invalid_payload", "...")` can become a throw, and no other change is needed for the person to see the right thing.
- **Plates pane:** the menu actions get wrapped in `reported(...)`. A failed result from the workspace becomes a throw instead of the "Couldn't do that" dialog.

Three groups are exceptions:

1. **Tool errors written for the AI model stay where they are.** The printer chat's action cards, the slice estimate, undoing a change and the All settings panel fall here. The model can act on that text, so it is an expected error for the model. Only the display changes: the person sees that the action failed, without the text. That's a change in how the page draws a failed card, not in the sites.

2. **`handshake_required` isn't a failure at all.** The native side restarted and forgot the page, and the page shakes hands again by itself and recovers. My view is that it should be plain control flow: no banner, no report, no text. Reporting it would send us an alert every time a normal restart happens.

3. **The messages that may be the person's to fix** stay as they are until Kenneth answers each one. Examples are the missing Bambu plug-in and a renamed printer.

One more point. A few `bridge_error` texts are already translated, such as "Another reply is currently streaming." and "Only the chat's last reply can be retried." Being translated doesn't make them expected errors. Both ends of that exchange are our code, so the page should never send those requests. If it does, that's a bug we need reported, not a sentence the person can do anything with.

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
description: "A failing test with a fake backend is not a reproduction; run the pre-fix code against the real thing before fixing, and say what was and was not seen"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A failing Catch2 test with a fake backend proves the code does what the brief says, not that the bug is real. Before fixing, run the code from before the fix against the real thing, with what the app actually knows printed beside what it says.

**Why:** on 2026-11-01 Kenneth asked whether I had reproduced three printer chat bugs, and I had only fakes for them: "I don't want you to fix the bugs that are in imagination only". The real run then showed one was only partly real as briefed: the "No printer in LAN mode" sentence was true of a printer in cloud mode.

**How to apply:** do it before writing the fix. To do it afterwards, swap production files with `git show <base>:<file>`, keep a temporary harness script, rebuild, and restore from `git show HEAD:<file>`. In zsh, loop over an array: a plain string variable does not split. Run harnesses with cwd in the scratchpad: the Bambu plug-in writes `log_iotc.txt` into the cwd. See [[printer-network-check-harness]].

# Brief: error messages people can do nothing about

Fix the error messages the app shows for failures the person can do nothing about. They are
listed in `i18n-unmarked-strings.md` and in the groups below. Work on a new branch from
`jusprin-dev`. Do not push, and add no merge commits.

The rule is in AGENTS.md under "Error handling". Read all of it before you start. A person sees a
specific sentence only when they can act on it and Kenneth chose that sentence. Every other
failure stops the work, goes up unchanged to the handler at the top of its entry point, and is
reported through `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`).
`report_unexpected_error` opens the dialog that says "Something went wrong on our side", so the
person sees only that. A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, and
its error text goes to the AI model only. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's
mistake, it is also sent through `report_if_automatic`.

Why these were missed: the earlier sweep (commit 3c134d39e3 on `jusprin-dev`, "Report every
failure a person cannot act on; keep a sentence only where they can") audited only
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `Home/`, plus the server. Nobody read `Shell/`, `Workspace/`
or `PrinterSetup/`. Read that commit's diff to see where it put top handlers (`reported(...)`).

## Remove the handling; don't swap the sentence

Do not replace each site's text with the generic sentence. That keeps a hundred places deciding
what the person sees, and most of them still send no report. Instead:

- Keep the check that notices the failure, and make it throw an error that carries the facts, for
  example "plate id 7 belongs to an earlier session". That text is for the report: it is not
  shown and not marked for translation.
- Let it travel to the top handler, which reports and opens the generic dialog. Show no second
  dialog of your own.

Top handlers that already exist:

- **Chat page messages.** `AgentWebView.cpp` (around line 314) catches anything thrown while
  handling a page message and calls `report_unexpected_error`. A `send_bridge_error(...)` in
  `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` for a request our own page should never send can become a throw.
  Being translated already (for example "Another reply is currently streaming.") does not make a
  message expected: both ends are our code, so a bad request is a bug.
- **Plates pane.** `LeftPane::run_command` (`Shell/LeftPane.cpp`) writes a log line and shows
  `result.message` under "Couldn't do that". A log line is not a report. Make a failed result a
  thrown error, and wrap the pane's actions in `reported(...)`.

Confirm every other path in the code, or in the running app, before you change it.

## Exceptions

1. **Text written for the AI model stays.** The printer chat's action cards, the setup card's
   slice estimate, undoing a change and the All settings panel are examples. The model can act on
   that text, so keep the sites. Change only the display, so the person sees that the action
   failed and not the text. Text such as "pass scope printer", "ask again with preempt" or "Read
   workspace_inspect", or the name "Orca", must not reach the person.
2. **`handshake_required` is not a failure.** The native side restarted and forgot the page, and
   the page shakes hands again by itself (`AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, `created.retry()`). Today the
   banner shows "A hello handshake is required before other messages." until dismissed. Check
   that the retry recovers. If it does, the person sees nothing and nothing is reported.
3. **Failures the person may be able to fix.** Build no sentence for these: each needs Kenneth's
   yes first. Leave each message as it is and bring it to Kenneth as one question, saying what the
   person would see and what they could do. Candidates:
   - "Connecting a Bambu Lab printer needs Bambu's network plug-in, which is not loaded"
   - "Could not start the client CLI. Use Copy or check its installation."
   - "This printer was renamed or removed. Open it again from Printers."
   - "Object name cannot be empty" and "Object already has that name" (perhaps the rename box
     should refuse those names instead)
   - "No more plates can be added" (perhaps the add button should be greyed out instead)

## How to work

- **Reproduce each failure before fixing it.** Show what the person sees before and after the
  fix. Most of these failures happen only when our own code is wrong, such as a page sending a
  malformed message or a stale plate id, so clicking in the app cannot cause them. For those,
  a reproduction is a run of the real app or the shell harness, with the failing condition forced
  (an instrumented page sending the bad message, or the harness passing the stale id), and a
  screenshot of what the person sees. A failing unit test alone is not a reproduction. A failure
  you cannot reproduce even this way gets no fix; list it.
- Add a test for each fix that fails first and passes after.
- One commit per cause.
- Update JusPrin's catalogs with `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`,
  so the deleted strings leave `native/` and `pages/`. `scripts/run_gettext` is OrcaSlicer's and
  is not used here.
- Build with `-- -j4`, after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`.
- Run `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, the AgentUI and HomeUI vitest suites, and the shell
  harness modes that cover what changed (the plates pane, the printer chat, printer setup,
  Preferences › Agent). On `jusprin-dev`, five modes reportedly already fail: `--print-issues`
  (7), `--print-issue-readers` (8), `--printer-network-check` (2), `--printer-connect-skill` (3)
  and `--project-prompt-requests` (1 to 3). Run them on the base too before calling a failure new.
  `--printer-chat-sheet` sometimes crashes while shutting down, on `jusprin-dev` too.
- Run `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` against `jusprin-dev`. On this Mac it failed to configure on
  2026-11-19 with "Could NOT find LibLZMA". If it still does, find why rather than skip it; if it
  cannot be made to run, say so, and check the includes of each changed file by hand.
- Never drive Kenneth's own JusPrin. Use a scratch `--datadir`. Send nothing to the real Sentry.

person sees only that. A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, and
its error text goes to the AI model only. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's
mistake, it is also sent through `report_if_automatic`.

Why these were missed: the earlier sweep (commit 3c134d39e3 on `jusprin-dev`, "Report every
failure a person cannot act on; keep a sentence only where they can") audited only
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `Home/`, plus the server. Nobody read `Shell/`, `Workspace/`
or `PrinterSetup/`. Read that commit's diff to see where it put top handlers (`reported(...)`).

## Remove the handling; don't swap the sentence

Do not replace each site's text with the generic sentence. That keeps a hundred places deciding
what the person sees, and most of them still send no report. Instead:

- Keep the check that notices the failure, and make it throw an error that carries the facts, for
  example "plate id 7 belongs to an earlier session". That text is for the report: it is not
  shown and not marked for translation.
- Let it travel to the top handler, which reports and opens the generic dialog. Show no second
  dialog of your own.

Top handlers that already exist:

- **Chat page messages.** `AgentWebView.cpp` (around line 314) catches anything thrown while
  handling a page message and calls `report_unexpected_error`. A `send_bridge_error(...)` in
  `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` for a request our own page should never send can become a throw.
  Being translated already (for example "Another reply is currently streaming.") does not make a
  message expected: both ends are our code, so a bad request is a bug.
- **Plates pane.** `LeftPane::run_command` (`Shell/LeftPane.cpp`) writes a log line and shows
  `result.message` under "Couldn't do that". A log line is not a report. Make a failed result a
  thrown error, and wrap the pane's actions in `reported(...)`.

Confirm every other path in the code, or in the running app, before you change it.

## Exceptions

1. **Text written for the AI model stays.** The printer chat's action cards, the setup card's
   slice estimate, undoing a change and the All settings panel are examples. The model can act on
   that text, so keep the sites. Change only the display, so the person sees that the action
   failed and not the text. Text such as "pass scope printer", "ask again with preempt" or "Read
   workspace_inspect", or the name "Orca", must not reach the person.
2. **`handshake_required` is not a failure.** The native side restarted and forgot the page, and
   the page shakes hands again by itself (`AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, `created.retry()`). Today the
   banner shows "A hello handshake is required before other messages." until dismissed. Check
   that the retry recovers. If it does, the person sees nothing and nothing is reported.
3. **Failures the person may be able to fix.** Build no sentence for these: each needs Kenneth's
   yes first. Leave each message as it is and bring it to Kenneth as one question, saying what the
   person would see and what they could do. Candidates:
   - "Connecting a Bambu Lab printer needs Bambu's network plug-in, which is not loaded"
   - "Could not start the client CLI. Use Copy or check its installation."
   - "This printer was renamed or removed. Open it again from Printers."
   - "Object name cannot be empty" and "Object already has that name" (perhaps the rename box
     should refuse those names instead)
   - "No more plates can be added" (perhaps the add button should be greyed out instead)

## How to work

- **Reproduce each failure before fixing it.** Show what the person sees before and after the
  fix. Most of these failures happen only when our own code is wrong, such as a page sending a
  malformed message or a stale plate id, so clicking in the app cannot cause them. For those,
  a reproduction is a run of the real app or the shell harness, with the failing condition forced
  (an instrumented page sending the bad message, or the harness passing the stale id), and a
  screenshot of what the person sees. A failing unit test alone is not a reproduction. A failure
  you cannot reproduce even this way gets no fix; list it.
- Add a test for each fix that fails first and passes after.
- One commit per cause.
- Update JusPrin's catalogs with `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`,
  so the deleted strings leave `native/` and `pages/`. `scripts/run_gettext` is OrcaSlicer's and
  is not used here.
- Build with `-- -j4`, after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`.
- Run `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, the AgentUI and HomeUI vitest suites, and the shell
  harness modes that cover what changed (the plates pane, the printer chat, printer setup,
  Preferences › Agent). On `jusprin-dev`, five modes reportedly already fail: `--print-issues`
  (7), `--print-issue-readers` (8), `--printer-network-check` (2), `--printer-connect-skill` (3)
  and `--project-prompt-requests` (1 to 3). Run them on the base too before calling a failure new.
  `--printer-chat-sheet` sometimes crashes while shutting down, on `jusprin-dev` too.
- Run `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` against `jusprin-dev`. On this Mac it failed to configure on
  2026-11-19 with "Could NOT find LibLZMA". If it still does, find why rather than skip it; if it
  cannot be made to run, say so, and check the includes of each changed file by hand.
- Never drive Kenneth's own JusPrin. Use a scratch `--datadir`. Send nothing to the real Sentry.

Kenneth, 2026-11-15, on the two tables shown to him in chat: "This table looks good. Confirmed." The rule in AGENTS.md asks for his yes on every entry and his words in the commit message; these are the words. The code that held the tables was deleted the same day ([[desktop-app-error-reports-default-on]]); copies of the deleted files are in `error-sweep-trial/deleted-build-session-2026-11-15/`.

**Desktop app, failed AI requests** (cause → what the person sees → next step):
- App older than the server serves → "This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts." → Get the new version
- Sign-in ended, or own API key rejected → "Their sign-in has ended, or the API key was rejected." → Sign in again, or update the key
- Out of credits → "They are out of credits." → Get more credits
- Chat larger than the AI service accepts → "The request was too large for the AI service." → none shown today
- Provider or our server limiting speed → "The AI service is rate limited." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider overloaded → "The AI service is overloaded." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider down or unreachable from our server → "The AI service is temporarily unavailable." → Retry
- Provider too slow, or connection stalled → "The AI request timed out." → Retry
- No network → "The AI request could not reach the service." → Check the network, then Retry

**Server, expected answers:**
- Signed out → "Sign in to JusPrin to continue." → Sign in again
- Out of credits → "This message needs N credits; you have M." → Get more credits (the table first shown to him said "You do not have enough credits for this message.", which the server never sent; asked which to keep on 2026-11-15, he took the pick, what the server sends: "Go with your picks for both")
- App too old → "This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts. Get the new version to keep using your account." → Get the new version
- Too many turns a minute, or provider limiting us → "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again." → Wait and retry
- Server's slots for large requests all taken → "JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment." → Retry
- Provider down, overloaded or unreachable → "The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly." → Retry
- Provider too slow → "The model service took too long to answer." → Retry
- Chat or report photos too large → "The request is too large." → New chat, or fewer pictures
- Print report too short → "A report needs a few sentences." → Write more
- Print report has no photo → "A report needs a photo of the printed object." → Add a photo
- Report photo cannot be opened → "That photo could not be read." → Add a different photo
- Print already reported → "This print already has a report." → Nothing

Also confirmed by the same answer: a provider's own "overloaded" event partway through a reply (Anthropic `overloaded_error`, OpenAI `server_is_overloaded`) counts as the "unavailable" entry and is not reported. The server table is in code since 2026-11-15: `web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py` `EXPECTED` (commits 057ea6d412, then the credits correction).

The second column is as shown to him: the app column is the build session's description of the sentence, not always the literal on-screen string, so check each against the code when rebuilding. The server's four other answers (invalid_request, unknown_model, method_not_allowed, upstream_error) stay unexpected: "Agreed. Treat them as unexpected errors." Note that at the last commit a provider's 400 or 422 is answered as invalid_request, which is the shape of the 2026-11-14 incident. The designed refusals outside AI requests (81 rows, not 89; `error-sweep-trial/designed-refusals-outside-ai-requests.md`, sorted in `designed-refusals-sorted.md`): on 2026-11-15 Kenneth decided the eleven that are failures with a sentence of their own and no named cause (rows 10, 11, 16, 21, 39, 54, 55, 58, 59, 60, 71) become unexpected errors: "Yes, go with this approach." A session converted 11, 16, 39, 55, 71 (on jusprin-dev in b3eed3bf4b) and asked him whether 10, 21, 54, 58, 59, 60 stay. Asked "Should the six failure sentences that session left alone stay as they are?", he answered the same day: "Yes, keep them". So those six keep their sentences (projects folder unreadable x2, "Signing in didn't finish", another app's settings file unreadable, "hasn't loaded the AI models yet", "The open project couldn't be saved"). The session's new on-screen strings (report rows App / Was doing / Where, the singular forms, the Preferences box text) were put to him in full the same day and he answered: "approved". The other 17 not-on-a-board rows are real named causes, not yet entered or confirmed.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

name: printer-prompt-card-wording-breaks-connect
description: "Bambu connect invented deviceIds because the app dropped tool results between turns; FIXED on jusprin-newui 115e2776bf (tool calls replayed); run_prompt_tests.py now replays too (40/40)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f665746c-cfdb-4776-8406-cafeefecc864
  modified: 2026-09-24T04:14:16.760Z
---

Found 2026-09-24 on branch claude/printer-receipt-card, by recording the app's OpenAI requests through a local proxy (`JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`).

**The root cause.** Between turns, AgentHost sends only the messages' text. It sends no function calls and no function_call_outputs. In turn 1 the model calls printer_connection_status and learns `deviceId: FAKE001`, then says "I found one A1 mini". On "Yes, connect it" that result is gone, so a model that calls printer_connect without checking again invents an id (`<from_status>`, `A1 mini`, `<deviceId from printer_connection_status>`) and gets unknown_device. Fixed 2026-09-24 on branch claude/llm-tool-history-context-774814 by replaying the session's tool calls and results across turns (5/5 vs 0/5 in a live check): see [[printer-chat-tool-history-replay]]. run_prompt_tests.py on this branch still copies text-only history and needs the same replay.

**Rates**, from `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` (connect-bambu):
- Shipped prompt: about 64% (32 of 50).
- With a prompt line about the "Printer added" receipt card: 4 of 20.

The app-based runs agreed in direction. That line stays out.

**Why small prompt edits swing it (ablation, 2026-09-24, 60 to 90 runs per variant):**
- The model almost never looks the printer up again on "connect it" (0-15% of runs).
- A run passes only when its first reply happens to quote the display name "JusPrin Fake A1 mini", which the app accepts as an id: those runs pass about 87% of the time. The rest of the time the model rebuilds an id from the name, e.g. JUSPRIN_FAKE_A1_MINI.
- When the reply doesn't name the printer and the model doesn't look again, the run fails every time (0 of 129).
- Quoting the name is incidental style that any edit shifts: the shipped prompt names it in 83% of runs, neutral unrelated sentences in about 60%, the receipt line in 38%, and the full receipt change in 19%.
- Pinning the drop on particular words ("do not repeat its name") was inconclusive.

**The lightweight test:** run_prompt_tests.py uses only Python's stdlib plus node. It renders the prompt from printerInstructions.ts via render_prompt.mjs, sends printer_tools.json (guarded by a test in test_openai_responses_agent.cpp; regenerate with JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1), and copies the text-only history. 20 runs take about 20 s. The shell harness's --printer-connect-trials mode was built, then removed in favour of it.

**Why:** single app runs are single samples. 0/3 vs 3/3 was once over-read as "the shipped prompt works".

**How to apply:** judge printer prompt edits with run_prompt_tests.py, 20 or more runs per side. Add new cases there, not to the shell harness. See [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

**Addendum 2026-09-23 (branch claude/printer-connect-async):** the runner was
still only on claude/printer-receipt-card; copied into a scratchpad and given
cases for host failure wording, "skip", the wait length, and the full list.
Lesson: an edit to the *connect* rules ("enter the connection details
themselves in the printer settings") dropped the unrelated "show me the full
printer list" step from 94% (85/90) to 73% (66/90), and only when the Add
session's context carried the real 383-printer catalogue plus a network

**Note 1: `handshake_required`.** Only two things set `m_handshake` back to false after a page has shaken hands:
- A main-frame navigation: `AgentWebView.cpp:267`, on any URL that is not `about:` and not a dropped file. That happens on the first load and on the native Retry, which calls `reload()` at `:340`.
- A `hello_reject` (`AgentHost.cpp:1289`).

So the refusal needs a message from the old document after navigation has started, or a broken page. When it does happen, `retry()` (`bridgeClient.ts`) posts hello. The host sends `hello_ack` and full state, and the page reconnects on its own: it flashes the connecting pane, then resends the instructions and skills. # Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Where to Create Worktrees and Temporary Folders

This file is read by more than one coding tool, so each rule names the idea first and the tool-specific path second.

1. **Use the location your own tool already uses for worktrees.** Claude Code: `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`. Codex: `~/.codex/worktrees/`. If this session was started inside a worktree the tool created, put any further worktree beside it.
2. **Never create a worktree or a working folder in `~` or directly under `~/Projects`.** That includes sibling folders such as `<repo>-worktrees`. This holds for a different repo than the one the session started in: use that repo's tool-managed location (rule 1) or the scratch directory (rule 3).
3. **Short-lived worktrees, build output, logs, screenshots and scripts go in the session's scratch or temp directory** if the tool gives one (Claude Code names it in the session instructions). If it gives none, use a new folder under the system temp directory, not the home directory.
4. **Keep non-worktree files out of worktree folders.** Logs, screenshots and scripts do not belong beside the worktrees. They go in the scratch directory, or inside the one worktree they concern.
5. **Use absolute paths when creating a worktree.** A shell may reset its working directory between commands, and a path starting with `~` or `..` can land somewhere unintended.
6. **Say where it is.** After creating a worktree, tell the user its full path, and remove it and its branch when the work is finished and merged.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.

## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

```bash

cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --

# Linux
```

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.
- Before building against a dependency folder built earlier, such as the main checkout's `deps/build/arm64`, run `scripts/deps_current.sh <folder>`. It rebuilds the libraries whose `deps/` recipe changed since that folder was built.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.

### Terminology

- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.

### Editing rules

- Only edit `msgstr` — **never** change `msgid`, and never "fix" wrong English in the translation alone. Report the source string instead.
- Preserve exactly: placeholders (`%s`, `%d`, `%1%`, `%zu`, `%%`), every `\n` (count *and* position, including leading/trailing), leading/trailing spaces, HTML tags, `℃`, and the file's encoding and line endings.
- **Never reorder positional arguments** in a `c-format` string. If the msgid is `%d` then `%s`, that order must hold — swapping them breaks at runtime.
- `msgctxt` separates homonyms — always read it. `Back`/`Camera View` is the rear view of the 3D navigator, while `Back`/`Navigation` is the go-back button; `Top` exists in the *Alignment*, *Layers* and *Camera View* senses.
- When a string needs disambiguating, add context in the source (`_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`), don't work around it in the translation.
- A literal `%` inside a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format` will fail `msgfmt`. Fix it with a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source — do not mangle the translation or use `%%` in text that is never passed through printf.
- Plural entries: read `nplurals` from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (it is **not** always 2 — ja/ko/zh/th/vi use 1, ru/cs/pl/lt use 3, uk uses 4). Each form must be genuinely inflected for its quantity; repeating one sentence across all forms is a bug in Slavic/Baltic languages, though it is correct for Turkish and Hungarian.
- An entry whose `msgstr` equals its `msgid` is untranslated even though it is not empty; a plural entry with any empty form is likewise incomplete.
- Mark machine-produced translations with an `# AI Translated` translator comment. Don't add it to a human translation you didn't actually rewrite.
- When you can't be sure of a machine translation's meaning or UI wording, also add `# Needs human review: <what to check>`. Never use `fuzzy` for this — fuzzy entries are hidden from users.
- Don't reflow or re-wrap unrelated entries — keep the diff limited to the strings you changed.

### Verifying

- `scripts/run_gettext.bat --full` (Windows) regenerates the template, merges every catalog and compiles the `.mo` files. It must exit 0.
- Or check a single catalog with `msgfmt --check-format --check-header -o <out>.mo localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`. Without `--check-header`, msgfmt skips the placeholder check in plural forms.
- Fuzzy entries are not shown to users. If you correct one, clear its `fuzzy` flag, otherwise the fix never ships.
